description.value: Three self-catering log cabins set in a remote, scenic location 12km south of Atlin with views over glaciers, mountains, and lakes. The property also rents canoes and kayaks for exploring the surrounding waterways. Atlin itself is a tiny historic gold rush town at the end of a spur road off the Alaska Highway, making this a true wilderness destination.

address.value: Warm Bay Road, Box 368, Atlin, BC V0W 1A0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website confirms this is a seasonal (May–October) self-catering cabin property 12km south of Atlin on Warm Bay Road, with 3 log cabins. Phone and website match between OSM and the site. OSM tag internet_access=no confirms no Wi-Fi. No mention of bike storage, cycling amenities, or any bike-related services anywhere on the site. The website explicitly recommends renting a car in Whitehorse for access, suggesting the property is oriented toward car-based visitors.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Legitimate seasonal accommodation but located 12km from Atlin on a rural road, and the website recommends renting a car for access. Practicality for loaded touring cyclists is uncertain. Atlin itself is extremely remote (end of Hwy 7 spur off Alaska Highway), so demand from cycle tourists may be very limited.
enrichment_extras.notes: Seasonal operation only: May long weekend through October long weekend. Two smaller cabins share a seasonal shower house; only the Birch Mountain cottage has its own bathroom.
